title: The Cost of a Bad Hire

parts.visual:
You hire a bad Sales Director. Their salary is $100,000. Six months later, you fire them. Did that mistake cost you $50,000? NO. It cost you over $1,000,000.

The Hidden Costs:
1. Direct Costs: Salary, recruiting fees, and severance pay.
2. Opportunity Cost: The massive amount of revenue they failed to generate during those 6 months.
3. Cultural Damage: The time the CEO wasted managing them, and the A-Players who quit because they hated working with an incompetent boss.
parts.audio: Founders vastly underestimate the true financial and emotional destruction of a bad hire. In a fast-moving startup, a toxic or incompetent leader is not just a waste of a salary; they are an existential threat to the company's momentum.

questions.question: A startup hires a toxic Vice President of Engineering. Two senior engineers (who are A-Players) get frustrated with the VP's bad decisions and quit. What is the true cost of this bad hire?
options: The catastrophic loss of institutional knowledge. The startup must now spend 6 months replacing the VP AND the two brilliant engineers, completely stopping all product development.
The cost of buying new computers.
questions.correct_answer: The catastrophic loss of institutional knowledge. The startup must now spend 6 months replacing the VP AND the two brilliant engineers, completely stopping all product development.
questions.explanation: A bad manager will push your best talent out the door.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO talk about the 'Management Tax'. What is he complaining about?
questions.tts_text: I am spending 4 hours a day just cleaning up his messes. I have to double-check all his emails. I am basically doing his job for him, which means I am not doing my job as CEO.
options: The Opportunity Cost of Time. A bad hire forces the founder to become a micromanager. Every hour the CEO spends babysitting a bad employee is an hour they are not spending raising capital or closing major deals.
questions.correct_answer: The Opportunity Cost of Time. A bad hire forces the founder to become a micromanager. Every hour the CEO spends babysitting a bad employee is an hour they are not spending raising capital or closing major deals.
questions.explanation: You hire people to buy back your time. A bad hire steals your time.

questions.question: Why do founders often wait too long to fire a bad hire?
options: Because of 'Sunk Cost Fallacy' and ego. They spent months recruiting the person, and firing them means the founder has to admit they made a massive mistake to the rest of the company.
Because it is illegal to fire people.
questions.correct_answer: Because of 'Sunk Cost Fallacy' and ego. They spent months recruiting the person, and firing them means the founder has to admit they made a massive mistake to the rest of the company.
questions.explanation: Your ego will bankrupt your company.

questions.question: What happens to the 'Speed of Execution' when you have a bad hire on a small 5-person team?
options: It grinds to a halt. In a tiny startup, there is nowhere to hide. If 1 out of 5 people is failing, the entire machine loses 20% of its power, and the other 4 people have to carry the dead weight.
questions.correct_answer: It grinds to a halt. In a tiny startup, there is nowhere to hide. If 1 out of 5 people is failing, the entire machine loses 20% of its power, and the other 4 people have to carry the dead weight.
questions.explanation: Startups win on speed. Dead weight kills speed.
